· **Evidence slot:** 3 — network (KSI-CNA, SC-8 / CA-7) · **Track modules:** [A3](../compliance-track.html#module-a3-network-control-plane-slot-3), [B3](../implementation-track.html#module-b3-data-platform-modernization-books-0406)

## Scope

Where federal databases should live after the identity modernization of
Books 04–05. **Logical centralization (one authoritative source per fact)
is almost always correct; physical centralization is constrained by the
speed-of-light propagation floor.** Match each workload's consistency class
to a network transport class, use SD-WAN to close the addressable latency
gap, and use token-based security to consolidate without perimeter-driven
fragmentation.

## Learning objectives

- Distinguish logical from physical centralization and explain why
  conflating them causes unnecessary cost or fragmentation.
- Compute the physics floor for a fiber route (~200,000 km/s) and separate
  it from the addressable gap SD-WAN can attack.
- Classify workloads into the six consistency classes (strong/serializable,
  synchronous, async, bounded staleness, causal/CRDT, eventual) and pick a
  matching transport class.
- Design lean/fat traffic separation for database clusters (consensus
  heartbeats vs. backups/replication) with SD-WAN classification and DSCP
  marking.
- Explain how Entra token scope replaces the network perimeter as the
  primary database access control, enabling consolidation across segments.
- Design an SSOT architecture with one canonical source and multiple
  consistency-class projections.

## Key concepts

- The speed-of-light tax: physics floor vs. addressable gap (e.g., DC–LA
  27 ms floor vs. 65–90 ms observed).
- SD-WAN near-geodesic routing, FEC/packet duplication, traffic-class
  separation.
- The lean/fat design rule for replication topology.
- Six consistency classes mapped to transport classes; the federal workload
  classification table.
- "Physics Constrains, Token Liberates" and the other Federal Data
  Architecture Principles.
- SSOT: one truth, many projections.

## Reading sequence

Architecture/principles-shaped: consolidation premise → logical vs.
physical distinction → speed-of-light constraints → SD-WAN as the
database's network ally → token-based security as consolidation enabler →
consistency-to-transport matching → the five principles → NIST closure.

## Compliance hooks

SC-28 (TDE), SC-8 (TLS + Arc certificate), SC-5 (SD-WAN QoS / lean-fat),
SI-12 (SSOT retention), CA-3 (token-scoped exchange), SA-8, AU-9
(geo-replicated audit logs), CP-9, CP-10.

## Prerequisites

Books 01–03 (IPAM/DDI/PKI, SD-WAN/SASE) and Books 04–05 (SQL identity
migration, Entra tokens, Managed Identity).

## Labs

1. Measure RTT across simulated WAN links; compute physics floor vs.
   addressable gap; demonstrate the latency cost of strong-consistency
   reads over a high-latency link vs. bounded-staleness replica reads.
2. Configure DSCP marking to separate a bulk backup transfer from
   consensus/heartbeat traffic and show quorum stability under load.
3. Build a replication-lag monitor that redirects reads to the primary
   when a replica exceeds its staleness bound.

## Pitfalls the book calls out

- Globally distributed databases with strong consistency for all reads —
  the source of "mysteriously" high read latency.
- Operating without explicit consistency-class assignment (implicit
  strong-consistency-everywhere).
- Running lean and fat traffic on one path — backups delay quorum
  heartbeats and cause failover flapping.
- Maintaining the same fact independently in multiple systems instead of
  one canonical source with derived projections.
